fullPassage:
Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain.

(C) A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress.

(A) Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future.

(B) It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.

One study ④<u>demonstrated</u> a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② made → making: 분사구문으로 주절 보충 설명. 'Stress affects..., making us...'에서 능동=현재분사.
det.analysis:
✅ ① affects: 3인칭 단수 주어에 맞는 동사
❌ ② made: 분사구문 능동이므로 making이 적절 ←정답
✅ ③ healthy: 형용사, people 수식
✅ ④ demonstrated: 과거 시제 동사
det.tip: 분사구문: 능동=V-ing, 수동=V-ed. Stress makes → making

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ involving → involved: 'is involved in'은 수동태 구문. involving은 능동분사로 부적합.
det.analysis:
✅ ① smaller: 비교급 형용사
✅ ② resilient: remain + 형용사 보어
❌ ③ involving: be involved in(~에 관여하다) 수동태 ←정답
✅ ④ regulating: 전치사 of + 동명사
det.tip: be involved in = ~에 관여하다 (수동). involving = ~을 포함하는 (능동)

det.korean: ① experiencing → experienced: 'had experienced'는 과거완료. had + p.p.(과거분사) 필수.
det.analysis:
❌ ① experiencing: had + p.p.에서 과거분사 experienced 필요 ←정답

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ③ neglect(방치하다) → monitor(감시하다): 해마는 환경 안전성을 '감시'하지 '방치'하지 않는다.
det.analysis:

✅ ② stressful(스트레스를 주는): 원문 일치
❌ ③ neglect(방치하다): 원문은 monitor(감시하다) — 반의어 ←정답
✅ ④ chronic(만성적인): 원문 일치
det.tip: monitor(감시) ↔ neglect(방치). monitor the safety = 안전성을 감시하다

det.korean: ④ intermittent(간헐적인) → constant(끊임없는): 투쟁-도주 상태에 '끊임없이' 갇히는 것이지 '간헐적'이 아님.

questions.passage: Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain. A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress. Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future. It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.
